propositions: The hardening byte-equivalence oracle executes both production and copied legacy Pandoc subprocesses (884 times each), sharing live mutable conversion constants; mutating _PANDOC_TO to plain changed both digests identically, proving the copied oracle is coupled rather than independent.

Replacing the copied legacy subprocess call with immutable expected-output fixture preserves all 884 real production Pandoc invocations while eliminating 884 redundant legacy subprocesses, reducing runtime by 32.3s (49.4 percent) and matching standard fixture practice.
Schema v1 stored only one macOS-arm64 Pandoc SHA-256 as platform-independent, causing Ubuntu x86_64 CI jobs to reject the Linux binary hash against the macOS hash while macOS passed.

Schema v2 retains the complete platform-specific Pandoc fingerprint map (darwin-arm64 and linux-x86_64) with deterministic platform selection, version validation, and regeneration safety; unknown platform, version drift, or hash mismatch fail closed with diagnostics.
